correctness.rationale: Checked conditional nonacute angle at X=(x,0) using ordered pairs on all four rectangle edges. The disjoint contributing side pairings give A=2wh+6x(w−x)+2(L+R+G+H), and elementary integration yields the two s=x(r−x) branches separated at s=1. Integrating the short and long sides gives B and S; when r>2 integrating ΔA=−r(s−1)²/s+2(s−1)log s over central interval gives C. Since at most one angle is nonacute for a nondegenerate triangle (including collinear triples on a side), the factor three is correct. Expansion with r=2+ε,x=r/2+sqrt(ε)t yields ΔA≈−ε³t²(1−t²)², ∫_{−1}¹t²(1−t²)²dt=16/105 and final coefficient 4/945. Thin-limit expansion agrees. Independent direct Monte Carlo for six r values, square value 23/96, cusp high-precision coefficients and thin r=1000 corroborated; no infinite claim inferred from sampling.
residual_risks: Cancellation in C at very large r makes naive floating-point evaluation ill-conditioned; asymptotic is analytic rather than a floating-point extrapolation.

value.rationale: Exact probability for a natural continuous one-parameter geometric model, including a genuine change of analytic regularity at the aspect ratio when the product threshold x(r−x)=1 first becomes possible. The new 7/2 cusp and thin-limit constant are motivated sharp invariants, not restated square data.
residual_risks: Applies only to normalized-arclength boundary sampling and does not prove optimality for arbitrary convex domains.

final_claim: For three independent normalized-arclength points on the perimeter of any rectangle of aspect ratio r≥1, the strict acute-triangle probability equals 1−3[B(r)+S(r)+C(r)]/[4(r+1)³], with the stated elementary B,S, and hyperbolic C (zero for r≤2); beyond r=2 it differs from analytic continuation by (4/945)(r−2)^(7/2)+O((r−2)^(9/2)) and decays (3log r−3/2)/r²+O(log r/r³) as r→∞.
limitations: Cancellation in C at very large r makes naive floating-point evaluation ill-conditioned; asymptotic is analytic rather than a floating-point extrapolation.
